title: Record types, business processes, picklists, and dependent picklists
objectives: Explain a record type as a way to offer different picklist values and page layouts for different business processes on the same object.
Place the master picklist as the complete value list, then subset values per record type.
Use a dependent picklist so available values change with a controlling field, and preview with record types when both exist.
Refuse a new object or a new text field when the need is a different process, layout, or picklist subset.
diagnostic_question: Facilities wants residential vs commercial properties with different status values, different layouts, and a city picklist that depends on region. Is that two objects, two record types, or a dependent picklist—or all three ideas?
definition: A record type lets an object support different business processes, page layouts, and picklist values. Before creating record types, put every possible value in the master picklist—the complete list that any record type can use—then subset values per record type and assign layouts by profile. A dependent picklist limits values based on a controlling field; if record types exist, a dependent value is available only when it is in the selected record type and allowed for the controlling value. ([Create Record Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=creating_record_types.htm); [Define a Dependent Picklist](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_defining_field_dependencies.htm); [Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm))
why_it_matters: Teams clone objects for 'commercial vs residential' when a record type plus picklist subsets would do. Interviewers listen for master picklist versus record-type values, for layout assignment by profile and record type, and for dependent picklists that still honor record types.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a restaurant. The record type is which menu you sat down with—lunch or catering. The business process is the ticket stages that kitchen uses for that menu. The master picklist is every dish the restaurant knows how to cook. Each menu shows a subset. A dependent picklist is the wine list that appears only after you pick steak. The dining-room furniture (page layout) is assigned by menu plus who you are (profile). Do not build a second restaurant building for a second menu.
deeper_explanation: Create Record Types Help: include all possible values in the master picklist first. Creating a record type without cloning copies master values; you then customize values for that record type. Assign one layout to all profiles or a different layout per profile. ([Create Record Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=creating_record_types.htm))
Page layouts: the combination of the user's profile and the record type determines which page layout is displayed. ([Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm))

Dependent picklists: choose a controlling field and dependent field, then fill the matrix. Preview can use a record type because the record type controls controlling-field values, and both record type and controlling value determine dependent values. Some picklists and checkboxes cannot be controlling fields. ([Define a Dependent Picklist](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_defining_field_dependencies.htm))

Business processes (Sales process, Lead process, Support process, and similar) are the stage/status picklist wrappers used with record types on those standard objects. Exact process names and which objects have them are object-specific—Needs verification on the object in Setup rather than inventing a universal process catalog.

Record types are metadata. Records store which record type they use (business data). Changing record-type picklist availability does not rewrite historical values automatically. Do not use record types as a security model; profiles and permission sets still own object access (SEC).

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant: record type is the menu you sat down with, business process is that menu's ticket stages, master picklist is every dish the kitchen can cook, dependent picklist is the wine that appears after you choose steak, and page layout is the table setting assigned by menu plus guest type.
useful_mapping: record type → lunch vs catering menu
business process → ticket stages for that menu
record-type values → dishes printed on this menu
dependent picklist → wine list gated by the dish
page layout assignment → table setting from menu + guest profile
where_it_breaks: Record types are not security; a profile can still query fields not on the layout.
Not every object has a formal business-process setup object.
Global value sets shared across objects are a neighboring picklist topic—confirm current Help if asked.
Dynamic Forms can reduce how many layouts you need (DATA-009); the restaurant still has menus.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Record types give one object different processes, picklist values, and layouts. Fill the master picklist first, then subset per record type. Layouts are assigned by profile plus record type. Dependent picklists still require the value on that record type.

terminology.plain: A flavor of the same object for a process.
terminology.precise: Lets you offer different picklist values and page layouts (and, on some objects, a business process) for different kinds of records.
terminology.non_example: A second custom object CommercialProperty__c with the same grain.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record: one row; it stores which record type it uses.

terminology.plain: Every value the object can ever use.
terminology.precise: The complete list of picklist values that can be used in any record type. Add values here before creating record types.
terminology.example: Status values New, Occupied, Rehab, Sold all on the master.
terminology.non_example: Values that exist only in a Flow decision.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record-type values: the subset shown for one type.
terminology.boundary: Help: include all possible values first.

terminology.plain: The stage path used with a record type on some standard objects.
terminology.precise: Setup wrappers such as sales or support processes that define stage/status values for a record type. Object-specific—confirm in Setup.
terminology.example: A sales process assigned to an Opportunity record type.
terminology.non_example: A custom status picklist on a custom object without a Process setup object.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Path: a presentation of stages, neighboring.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent a process object for every custom object.

terminology.plain: A field whose values are chosen from a list.
terminology.precise: A data type (DATA-002) whose allowed values can be subsetted by record type and can control or depend on another picklist.
terminology.non_example: A Text field with suggested words.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Multi-select picklist: neighboring type with different dependency rules—Needs verification.
terminology.boundary: Master values live on the field.

terminology.plain: A picklist filtered by another field.
terminology.precise: Values available when the user selects a controlling field value; also gated by record type when record types exist.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Controlling field: the driver, sometimes a checkbox.
terminology.boundary: Not every picklist can be controlling.

terminology.plain: The field that drives a dependency.
terminology.precise: The field chosen first in the dependency matrix. Some picklist and checkbox fields are not available as controlling fields.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record type: also gates values, but is not the controlling field.
terminology.boundary: Confirm availability in the New Dependency wizard.

terminology.plain: Which layout a user sees for a record type.
terminology.precise: Assigned when creating a record type (one layout or per profile). Runtime: profile + record type.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning record page: another assignment layer (DATA-009).
terminology.boundary: Layout is presentation, not the record type itself.

terminology.precise: Business data: the record stores its record type. Changing available picklist values later does not always rewrite old values.
terminology.example: A LAB_ property saved as Commercial.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Default record type on a profile: who gets which default on create.
terminology.boundary: Conversion between types is a data operation.

when_to_use: When one object needs different picklist values, page layouts, or business processes for different kinds of records.
When you must maintain a master picklist and then subset values per record type.
When a picklist should depend on a controlling field and still honor record types.
When layout assignment must vary by profile and record type together.
When someone wants a second object but the noun and grain are the same.
when_not_to_use: Do not create a new object or schema when a record type and picklists can express the process difference.
Do not use record types as a substitute for field-level security or sharing.
Do not use a text field instead of a picklist when values must be controlled and subsetted.
Do not use a record type to calculate a value (formula) or to aggregate children (roll-up).
Do not add a dependent picklist value that is missing from the record type and expect it to appear.
configuration_or_code_location: Object Manager → Record Types; Picklist field value set (master).
Record type creation: layout assignment by profile.
Profiles: default record type and available record types.

limitations: Standard business-process object list is not exhaustive here.

Record types do not replace sharing.
security_notes: Hiding a field on a layout is not FLS.
Available record types on a profile control create options, not record-level access.
Do not use record types to hide confidential fields from API users.
common_mistakes: Cloning the object for a second process.
Expecting a dependent value that is not on the record type.
Using text instead of picklists for controlled values.

interview_questions.question: What is a record type, and how do picklists relate?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A record type is a process-and-layout flavor of one object. The master picklist holds every value; each record type subsets those values. Layouts are assigned by profile plus record type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse object clones when the noun matches. I fill the master list first. I mention dependent picklists as a second filter on top of record types. I do not call record types a security model. I mention business processes on some standard objects as Needs verification by object.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Property__c Residential vs Commercial with different Status values.
weak_answer_warnings: Defining record type as a new object

interview_questions.question: Commercial vs residential properties—two objects?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No, if grain is the same. Use two record types, subset picklists, and assign layouts. Build a second object only if the noun or relationships truly differ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask whether units, vendors, and fields are the same shape. If yes, record types. I add Region→City dependency. I assign Finance vs Facilities layouts on Commercial. I do not use types as FLS for a confidential field.
interview_questions.example: Rejected LAB_CommercialProperty__c; created two record types on LAB_Property__c.
follow_ups: How do reports filter by record type?

interview_questions.question: How do dependent picklists interact with record types?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A dependent value appears only if the record type includes it and the controlling value allows it. Preview both gates.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I fill the matrix, then I include cities on each record type that should see them. A city on the master but not on Commercial will not appear for Commercial even if East allows it. I mention some fields cannot be controlling.
interview_questions.example: Preview Commercial + East shows only cities in both gates.
follow_ups: Do multi-selects depend the same way?

interview_questions.question: Finance and Facilities need different Commercial screens.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Assign different page layouts to those profiles for the Commercial record type. Do not create a third record type that means the same process unless the values also differ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Create Record Types allows one layout for all profiles or a layout per profile. Runtime uses profile + record type. DATA-009 may add a Lightning page layer. I still keep one Commercial type if the process is the same.
interview_questions.example: Commercial + Finance layout hides operational fields; Facilities layout shows them.
tradeoffs: Per-profile layout vs extra record type
follow_ups: What if they need different picklist values too?
Is compact layout assigned the same way?
weak_answer_warnings: Creating Finance-Commercial as a new object

interview_questions.question: A new Status does not appear on Residential.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Add it to the master picklist if it is missing, then include it on the Residential record type. Creating a new type is the wrong first move.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the Status field's value set, then Record Type picklist maintenance. I test a LAB_ Residential record. I do not convert Status to Text. Historical records keep old values until updated as data.
interview_questions.example: Added Rehab to the master list and to Residential only.
follow_ups: What happens to old records using a deactivated value?
Does API ignore record-type value subsets? Needs verification.

interview_questions.question: City is blank on a Commercial record even though East is set.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check whether that city is on the Commercial record type and whether the dependency matrix allows East→city. Also check the layout includes City.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Preview with Commercial selected. I do not start with sharing. If they typed city as Text, I convert to a dependent picklist. If a formula should display parent city, that is DATA-006, not this picklist.
interview_questions.example: Preview showed city missing from Commercial; adding it to the type fixed the UI.
tradeoffs: Type gate vs matrix gate vs layout
follow_ups: How do you migrate text cities?

interview_questions.question: Are record types a security tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. They change available values and which layout is assigned. Field-level security and sharing still decide what an API or user can access.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I say a profile can query a field that is not on the layout. Record types available on a profile control which types you can create. I would not hide salary with a record type. SEC topics own authorization.
interview_questions.example: Salary still readable via API despite being off the Commercial layout.
follow_ups: What does default record type on a profile do?
Can permission sets grant record types?
weak_answer_warnings: Promising record types hide fields from reports and API

interview_questions.question: When is a business process part of the answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: On objects that have a formal process setup—commonly Opportunity stages, Lead status, or Case status—assigned to a record type. Custom objects usually use an ordinary picklist plus record types.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not invent a Process object for LAB_Property__c. I subset the Status picklist per type. If the interviewer says Opportunity, I mention a sales process assigned to the record type and then verify the current Setup name. I keep Path as presentation.
interview_questions.example: Opportunity record type New Business assigned a sales process; LAB_Property__c uses a Status picklist only.
follow_ups: Can two types share one process?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying every object has a sales process
